Globe 540 Piece 3D Puzzle Ball I love geography and travel, and putting this together is both fun in a puzzle sort of way and great for reminiscing about past travels and dreaming about places yet to be seen in person. It's really cool - even cooler that it comes with a stand and you have a globe of your own afterward.

It is very up to date - it includes S. Sudan. And a warning to independence haters: Kosovo is shown as its own country. It is quite small and not labeled, but it has its own color.

We did the first half (the bottom) in the first night, but used the numbered backs as a guide as shown on the instruction sheet. It was fun, but left something to be desired. I wished they didn't have the numbers, and thought they would be impossible to ignore. After this, this was going to be the first Ravensburger puzzle I would have given less than five stars.

BUT the second night we finished it, but without the numbers. Turns out they were easy to ignore, and this allowed it to be what it should have been all along.

It might be overwhelming to not look at the numbers at first, but I suggest you do it that way. I suspect you still will have it done in 3-4 nights (assuming a few hours each night - it is addicting).

The pieces are plenty durable for snapping together, but many pieces are alike, so you could conceivably put the whole thing together as a sphere, but have it still be wrong. Anyone with any sense of geography would be able to catch a mistake like that. And when in doubt, the backs are numbered.

And when you're done, you have a nice little globe, textured to show it was a puzzle, and with a reasonably good looking stand. Very neat.
text_fidelity_b: Globe 540 Piece 3D Puzzle Ball

Sometimes that doesn’t work so well with kids. It also takes adult supervision from beginning to end. You’ll want to either have an apron, or clothes you don’t mind getting dirty. But it’s chocolate, so most kids love chocolate, no matter what!

This is a “simple” item that uses hot water to melt the chocolate. That’s not always going to work. It can depend upon the type / brand of chocolate you use. The chocolate is not included. Again, this is all part of the “experimentation” process. Make sure your hot water is really hot. Fill the melting container. . . Shake it around for a couple of minutes. . . Empty the container. . . then fill it back up with hot water again. . . before placing the chocolate into the container.

The current cost isn’t “crazy expensive” for a Made in China set. . . And it can give you an afternoon of fun with your children, so, in the end, I think it’s worth it.

And if a child ever accidentally fired the discs in the direction of another child's eyes, although I don't think that they will be injured, they will at least hear it coming. (3) The armband and handgrip are perfect for holding the shield. And (4) it seems like fun. While my 10 year old (it was his birthday today) had fun, I do think that a slightly younger child (7 or 8) would have more fun and not become bored as quickly as an older one.

text_fidelity_a:
Fisher-Price Connect Digital Soother We are using this soother with an 8 month old who generally sleeps very well.

Pros - Easy to use and the sounds, volume control, and lighting are well done.

Cons- Expensive, goes through batteries fast, not that interesting to our baby. He watches it for a short time and then loses interest (just as well if you are putting him to sleep). The biggest problem is that our machine goes to sleep after a short while and then won't restart.

Nothing compares to the old Fisher-Price Rainforest soother from 10 years ago that had water in it. My first grandson loved it and it lasted for years.

I agree with an earlier reviewer that the Cloud B Sleep Sheep is a better buy for providing the soft white noise that both soothes your baby and masks other sounds in the house. All five of my grand kids have some kind of sound machine in their bedroom, ranging from the $26 sheep to a $100 Ecotones Sound + Sleep Machine (I've bought five of those for adult family members).

I also think the kids go to sleep quicker and sleep more soundly in a totally dark room with no visual stimulation.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Connect Digital Soother

Stored inside are two snakes (drumsticks), two giraffes (maracas/rattles), a hornbill (water whistle--you fill with water in the hole in the head, then blow on the whistle for a warble sound), an antelope (slide whistle--you blow in the whistle while sliding the legs in and out to change the tone), and a crocodile (cabasa-clacker--you rotate the handle to make the drum play itself).

text_fidelity_a:
Mountains Out of Molehills | Family Board Game for 2-4 Players | Two-Level Gameboard Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Great Gateway Game for Ages 9+ This game hits that sweet spot where the complexity is enough for adults but not so high that kids struggle. And it’s FUN! It says 9 and up but my 7-year-old caught on pretty quickly and was delighted when we talked about it in terms of executing a program. My family loves this game. My husband and I can see playing it with just adults too.

The gameplay involves drafting cards and then using them to create a plan for how the mole will move on the grid, which is essentially a simple program much like one would write on a computer. It takes some strategy, but you can only predict other people so much and this is where the game shines.

I was worried it would be too complex or long when we read the rules, but it plays very smoothly! We felt comfortable within 2 rounds, and it was a lot of fun seeing how the plans we made would be thwarted as other players move. We also enjoyed how the turn order changed. There are many levels of subtle strategy, I feel like we will be learning new things each time we play. There is a random element of dice when placing a rock on the board, simple but genius game design. It keeps it from feeling unfair, and adds an element of luck to using it.

Even when you are losing, it’s so interesting to see the programs unfold as each card flips that it didn’t feel upsetting, and most of the points are earned in the later rounds as the mounds get higher so you can easily catch back up to an early lead or after a bad round. This means you don’t feel too discouraged if you have a poor start.

I like that it has a defined timeline, there are 6 rounds and you know what they will look like. Overall a great choice for a family game night as it is not likely to overrun an hour.

The double-layer boards and gameplay are unique and the story of the moles is full of flavor. The art is charming and the explanation of the rules such as “moles are too polite so they don’t move when they hit another” is a really sweet touch. The printing is great quality, the game is just beautiful to look at. The box is well-organized making setup and takedown easy, and it looks pretty on the shelf. Plus, we love the moles! The standees make great pieces. This game shows a lot of care in the details, and we love games with a lot of artistic flavor.

We play a lot of games as a family, but when we finished this one kiddo said this was their new favorite! The only downside is the limit of 2-4 players–it keeps it moving but means we can’t invite more friends to play at a time!

Bonus, the box art is beautiful so this also would make a lovely gift to open.
text_fidelity_b: Mountains Out of Molehills | Family Board Game for 2-4 Players | Two-Level Gameboard Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Great Gateway Game for Ages 9+

text_fidelity_a:
Paw Patrol Mission Chase Figure (Due to the malfunctions on our particular dog, and the fact that he doesn't walk at all, I was tempted to give it 3 stars, but he's so cute and fun, I went with 4.)

I have a few Paw Patrol fans in my house, so this is a pretty amazing toy.

By pressing the badge on the front of Chase, your children are given a mission. Chase talks and interacts through these missions. For example, chickens have gotten loose, and your child needs to help gather them up. The net compartment opens up, and your child will fire the net out. Chase comments on catching one, and then asks for the net to be reloaded. (One time the net got stuck, and didn't fire out, but he still exclaimed praise at catching a chicken, so it's not perfect.) He won't interact to various things that your child says, but he does have built in interaction, which is still pretty cool.

There are 24 different missions, and Chase moves around a bit through these. I was expecting him to walk a bit, but he never did. He just moves his head around, and moves from crouching to standing positions. There are two compartments on his backpack. One has a net launcher. The other has a microphone(that your child can talk into) and a flashlight. There are various buttons for each feature. (One for opening each compartment, one on the net launcher to launch, one to make the light come on the flashlight, and one to turn on the microphone.) Some of the items come on automatically through missions, but others require your child's assistance, when Chase asks.

Although this is an awesome toy that I'm pretty sure any Paw Patrol fan will love, we did have a couple of negatives with ours.

When the box was first opened, the head was detached a bit, but thankfully, it went back on pretty easily. Also, the button to launch the microphone/flashlight wouldn't work. I tried everything I could to make it work, short of tearing it apart, and tried numerous times, but it never worked. It didn't work when it was supposed to automatically open during missions, either. Thankfully, we can just pull that compartment open. During missions when a child is asked to launch the microphone/flashlight, pulling open the door makes the task recognized, just as if the button worked. So, it's not a huge deal, but still disappointing.

I really do wish he walked a bit, too! The way he's designed, it looked as if he would.

A couple of notes:
-This toy DOES come with batteries, but require 4 AA if you'd like to buy extras.
-If your child can read, know that the box this is delivered in says what's inside, though there are no pictures.
text_fidelity_b: Paw Patrol Mission Chase Figure

text_fidelity_a:
Baby Alive My Baby All Gone Doll, Blonde Baby Alive is an iconic doll. She was one of the first dolls that not only took a bottle, but also ate food, mixed and served to her from premade packets. She has been available in many different versions, each with the same eat/drink concept with a slightly different variation. My Baby All Gone is one of the latest Baby Alive dolls and she will easily keep your little one serving, feeding, changing, and burping her baby for hours.

What sets this Baby Alive doll apart from most of the others in the series is her ability to say so many different things. She still takes a bottle, eats food, pees, and poops just like the other Baby Alive dolls, but for a more realistic twist, she makes periodic statements from her wee little mouth. She will say that she wants to cuddle, that she just went pee, and so on. Her baby- ish voice and cute sayings will appeal strongly to young girls still going through their mommy phase.

My girls are both in their early years of elementary school, but they still like dolls and they like Baby Alive My Baby All Gone Doll just as much if not more than the others in the series, of which they have quite a few dolls. What they like best is the feature that sets this doll apart: The sayings, mentioned above. They like that she says so many different things- more than 30 sayings in all- because it makes her seem more real. I agree that the multitude of sayings is a vast improvement on other dolls that, while they might speak, say only three or four different things. My girls like playing the role of mommy, changing diapers, giving Baby Alive a nap, and everything else that goes with being a mom.

The one disadvantage of this Baby Alive doll is the same disadvantage with the others- you have to constantly purchase refill packs. Trust me, the few packs of food and the small number of diapers will not last long at all! In a matter of a day or two out of the package, your girls will be asking for replacement food and diapers. We have had this doll in our household for only about 10 days and have already ordered a refill pack.

Little girls often like to play the role of a mommy and Baby Alive is one of the best dolls for interactive mommy play. My girls like her very much and I like that they are happy. The cost of the refill packs can add up, so try to improvise when you can or create your own cloth diapers that can be washed and reused. Then watch as the young girl in your household practices her mommy role with a doll that, while not alive, is about as close as you can get to the real thing.
text_fidelity_b: Baby Alive My Baby All Gone Doll, Blonde

It's just about impossible to inflate or deflate because of the valves; standard foot pumps do not work with these valves and doing it by mouth (which is what I ended up doing) is extremely tedious, because there is not enough length to hold it in your mouth to pinch it for opening the valve. text_fidelity_a: Barbie Dreamtopia Sweetville Kingdom Carriage I have been a Barbie fan since I was a child, many years ago. My now 16 year old daughter was a huge fan when she was young. I even have several "in the box" collector Barbies. The Barbie Dreamtopia Sweetville Kingdom Carriage just doesn't seem as high quality as the many Barbie products I have purchased over the years. It's definitely not a collector's item. The price is decent and you get a complete set of a doll, unicorn, and carriage. The plastic carriage flexes when you apply pressure. It doesn't feel like it's going to easily break, but it's not as rigid as other Barbie products. The carriage door opens and closes.  The wheels rotate easily and give a pretty smooth ride. The details on the carriage are nice. There are lots of textures to make it more realistic.  The unicorn is a sturdier plastic piece. The doll has the rigid, no bend legs. Her facial details are what you expect on Barbies. She has a removable crown. Her top is molded plastic and not removable. Her skirt is a cute, candy print fabric, but the material itself is stiff and doesn't flow or move. In fact, I don't like the skirt at all. Overall, it's an attractive looking set, but the quality is disappointing. With all that said, I think young Barbie fans would probably still enjoy it.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Dreamtopia Sweetville Kingdom Carriage

Friendly Loom 7" Potholder Kit Green Metal Loom and Bright Rainbow Color Cotton Loops, Makes 2 Potholders, MADE IN THE USA by Harrisville Designs. I had almost forgotten about this little loom -- I first learned how to make these potholders in the 1950s even before I started school (I was probably 5 yrs old). My brother and I spent many summers working on these and selling them around the neighborhood to augment our $0.25/week allowance. My mother taught us how to make them and kept us supplied with the loops while we came up with our own designs.

One thing I remember very clearly -- she avoided nylon loops, preferring instead cotton loops. Why? Because the nylon loops could melt at the temperatures commonly encountered when using cast iron pans and metal baking dishes in hot ovens. I retained that memory, so when I saw this kit available with cotton loops, I knew I needed to try it one more time.

The major difference I see is in the length of the "prongs" in the loom -- I recall them being a little longer. Also, the metal weaving hook was a bit longer. But other than that, the design and construction are close to what I used as a child.

The package from Amazon arrived earlier today, and I quickly put together the potholder in the photo. It took probably an hour -- perhaps a bit longer, but not much. There are enough loops for a couple of pot holders and enough colors to mix and match. Follow the directions, especially the part about finishing -- pulling one of the loops on each finished edge back over a loom peg to keep the rest of the loops on the adjacent and opposite sides from popping off the loom. Take your time with this part -- it's easy to want to hurry to finish it, but it can be a bit "fiddly."

Very happy with this -- I've already ordered additional loops in specific colors to coordinate with my kitchen colors so I can make several of these to use as potholders as well as hot pads/trivets.
text_fidelity_b: Friendly Loom 7" Potholder Kit Green Metal Loom and Bright Rainbow Color Cotton Loops, Makes 2 Potholders, MADE IN THE USA by Harrisville Designs.

This is a painting of a whole bunch of pictures and other scenes and people from the 1980's. It's based on a painting by Jim Mellet, and his art is amazing! It takes a ton of scenes and people from the 1980's, and turns it into a wonderful painted collage.

The quality of the puzzle is top-notch. The pieces are very thick, and so they fit together well. The backing is a nice blue color, so you can easily tell which pieces are upside down. The border is awesome. The puzzle is surrounded by a red and orange line. This makes the border really easy to put together, and it makes it very easy to identify the edge pieces.

The puzzle is challenging, but it's also very doable. In most puzzles, there's a huge spot of the same color that's very boring, and this puzzle didn't have any of this. I felt entertained and challenged throughout. It's also a great conversation starter, because it has so many iconic people and scenes. I especially liked the Atari, Donkey Kong, Pac-Man, and Mr. T.

text_fidelity_a:
Legacy Deluxe Mancala Classic Game with Folding Wooden Game Board and Colored Glass Stones, Family Game for Ages 8 and up Chess has been my favorite board game since I was a child and I have collected chess sets as a hobby over the years. When I selected this one I expected it to be on par with typical portable wooden sets which are usually cheaply made. This one was a pleasant surprise in that it is a step up from most portable wooden sets I have seen and used.

This is a fairly straightforward set. The case is a clamshell design that folds open into the board. There are magnets in the rim of the underside of the board to hold it closed when the set is not in use, ands the manufacturer did a decent job of concealing the contacts (though they are visible if you look for them). The squares on the board are smooth and while the seams between the squares can be felt when you run your hand along the board, the seams are smooth and are less pronounced that what I have seen on some other boards.

The pieces are decently made though are nothing special. They are machine cut pieces and have been smoothed, sanded and varnished. They are weighted nicely and have felt on the bottom to avoid scratching the board. They’re a fairly average design but they look good and are very recognizable.

The main feature of this set is that it is larger than most fold-out boards I have seen and used. While this might not be the best for packing and portability, I really like the size. I am less likely to knock over pieces accidentally and I can see what’s going on a little better.

This is not just a chess set but includes wood chips for playing checkers as well. The chips are small and are nothing of note but they are sufficient.

I really like this chess set and will use it as my main travel set moving forward. I like the size of the board, the feel of the pieces and the overall quality. There are better sets out there but they cost more. There are less expensive sets too, and the chances of finding one that is of the same quality as this one for less is small.

text_fidelity_a: 4M T-Rex Dinosaur DNA Kit, 4945, Multi What kid doesn't like dinosaurs?  This is perfert for your boy or girl who is into dinosaurs.  I suppose it could be considered an educational toy, but probably only marginally so.  Who says educational toys can't be fun too?  This is especially nice for a kid interested in archeology.  Contains a block of plaster that has embedded into it "DNA" stickers and a glow in the dark dinosaur.  After the fun of digging out the dinosaur and stickers with the included digging tools and brush, they are left with a dinosaur model, so even though the digging fun is over after one time (if they do it all at once), there is something to show for it.  There are also two "augmented reality" (AR) play mats that are completed with the DNA stickers that have been "excavated".  The mats when used with a cell phone and an application from the App Store (for Apple phones) or the Google Play Store (for Androids) produces a 3D dinosaur, visible on the phone.  One problem with this is that it might not work with all cell phones.  It is supposed to work with MOST Apple devices (8.0 and above).  On Android phones the only devices tested are Google Nexus Series, Samsung Galaxy S5 and Samsung Galaxy Tab.  I didn't have a cell phone to test this on, but it seems like it still might be fun even if that part doesn't work.  It's just that you might not be able to use the full capability of the kit if your phone doesn't work with the application.  Also if you give this to a child of only 8 (the lower age limit on this), they may not yet have a cell and you may not want them to have one at that age.  Since this contains many small parts, it needs to be kept away from small children, as there is a choking hazard (box says no one under 3).  I would have loved a toy like this when I was a kid.  Just remember to put down a newspaper when they are working on the plaster block in order to collect all the plaster pieces that are chipped off as they excavate.  Pricing of the kit is very reasonable.  Made in China.
text_fidelity_b: 4M T-Rex Dinosaur DNA Kit, 4945, Multi

text_fidelity_a:
YIGO - Fun & Challenging Word Game for Clever Minds - Exciting Brain Game for Kids, Teens & Adults - Improves Spelling, Vocabulary & Memory - Educational Family Card Game for Boys & Girls [[VIDEOID:258489d4261f7a5b0f26535ccf27c4f9]] The plusses: The game is beautiful to look at and feels good quality. The print quality is very very good, these cards do not feel cheap, they feel almost like fancy plastic. It’s also a standard size which means if you are heavy users it’s not challenging to find sleeves to accommodate. I’m also pretty sure the box is big enough to handle sleeves. The rules are relatively simple, and the instruction manual provides a QR code that leads to a video of the gameplay combined with errata to the rules as written. You will *need* the errata because the rules do not answer very basic questions. It makes me wonder how much this was play-tested with strangers before release. It’s great to see a company offering solid support after release though!

At more than 100 cards, the deck is very unwieldy to shuffle, this is definitely one that needs to be broken into smaller piles to handle and then combined.

The rounds are much shorter than expected, some rounds were over in a 2 player game in as little as three fast turns. The actual gameplay is not one “game” but to have the least points over the series of many rounds (the most “loses” the game night.) There was very little tension or any emotional investment because of the fast turnover–that might work for some folks but it didn’t feel like it was worth working on big words without stalling. There were two rounds where the game was over in two turns before my husband could even play a card. It feels like more luck than skill which is not desirable in a word game. My biggest criticism is that due to the number of repeated vowels, gameplay can feel repetitive, we started round after round with “e” or “a” despite shuffling many times. I would love to see a second deck of a different color with starting letters distributed in a more logical way because the starting letter affects the gameplay variety over time. My husband and I love wordplay and puns as a rule and this game was not skill-based enough for the two-player version for us to want to invest too much more time on it. Maybe if we played it for longer there would be more to it but we both got bored after playing 10 or so rounds and probably wouldn’t give it a second try.

The idea itself is an awesome one, when it works it’s like combining scrabble with Uno. There is solid product quality and marketing. It just lacked the skill vs luck factor for us, which may be personal taste

I really think this game needs some tweaks to the gameplay to make it better before I’d really recommend it, at least on the game shelf of a couple. It says ages 8 and up, but I can’t imagine playing this with my almost 8yo, especially without eliminating some of the rules regarding “made up words” because 50 points penalty is pretty punitive for what might be an accidental misspelling, and even with some coaching it would be pretty difficult (And my kiddo has an above-average vocabulary). Maybe several 8yo together do well? We may try to break it out at a party among adults in the future.
text_fidelity_b: YIGO - Fun & Challenging Word Game for Clever Minds - Exciting Brain Game for Kids, Teens & Adults - Improves Spelling, Vocabulary & Memory - Educational Family Card Game for Boys & Girls

When opening, before you push the middle part of the bottom down, straighten and lock the side rails up. If you open it up all the way, the two smaller sides won't lock into place. Pull the red strap back up a bit then click them and push the bottom back down.

This is a cool novelty gift that is also educational, but it is not really helpful in learning a language unless you already know the letters, where applicable, and the pronunciation. It is not useful, for example, if you are traveling or trying to have even the most basic conversation.

The first two #1 bags build the planter, the three #2 bags build three succulents, and the three #3 bags build three more succulents and have round brown studs to simulate dirt.

I don’t like loose pieces, so I didn’t use the studs to mimic dirt. The planter is full without the studs, so I think that’s a matter of personal preference. The finished set fits right in with my other name-brand sets.

Niya - a game by Bruno Cathala I love to play games! Over the years we've played lots of party games and games for groups (may have something to do with having 6 kids), but now that we are empty nesters we have been looking for games for 2 players. We got this at a local games store and we absolutely love it!
I don't particularly like games that are super complex, where you have to read every card and figure out how it interacts with the other 200 cards. Niya can be explained in 5 minutes and played in 10-15 minutes, but it is also strategic.
The quality is excellent, with a great metal tin instead of a cardboard box, sturdy board pieces, and weighty playing pieces.
The artwork is very nice, with a clean, simple aesthetic. Very Japanese!
I have two very nit picky complaints about it. One of the categories on the board pieces is pines. They look very much like cacti to me. The other is that on the black pieces the black hair of the characters kind of disappears. I wish they had outlined them somehow.
All in all a great game. Highly recommended.

Hot Wheels 20-Pack of 1:64 Scale Toy Sports & Race Cars, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary) It might seem as if 20 cars is too much at once. Nope! It is wonderful.

Days as a five year-old were best filled with playing in complete abandon. The freedom proffered by youth needed only a few toys to complete the ever-present joy. A few toys which mattered included several tattered but friendly books, a truck or two, an odd shovel and bucket, and, the coup de grace, a Hot Wheels car. Mattel makes a track as well, but a well-made car could take a boy places. This set of 20 is what kindergartners drool over.

A boy has everything in this set: vehicles of all colors, a few truck varieties, some funny looking cars. There are plenty, and frankly, since a few will invariably wind up lost under the couch, eaten by the dog, and buried with other treasures in the garden, having 20 quickly becomes justified.

Why a Hot Wheels car? Because they are made with hard steel. They are painted with a slick color. They hold up to frequent tastings, sand grindings, dirt smearings and other nonsense that comes with power racing in a sandbox. Sticky chocolate wipes off with warm water, and grime comes out with a good spray under the faucet.

The wheels themselves have a bounce peculiar to a genuine Hot Wheels vehicle. That's how my brother and I made sure it had adequate fuel. Ten bounces should be enough, we figured, and usually, we were right.

I fully recommend the "Hot Wheels 20-Car Gift Pack."

Anthony Trendl
AmericanSpeechwriter.com
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels 20-Pack of 1:64 Scale Toy Sports & Race Cars, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary)

Fisher-Price Pop Superstar Minnie is a singing, dancing Minnie Mouse doll from Disney Junior whose skirt sways and spins 360° to the beat of her song as she lights up, sings and says fun phrases Many years ago, I worked for the mouse. Both of my grandkids grew up on Disney cartoons. Needless to say, both children had all kinds of Disney toys, clothes, movies, etc. This new Minnie Pop Superstar is adorable. I have pushed her button a number of times because she is too cute. She has over 20 sounds and phrases. Her skirt moves and she can twirl and dance, and there are lights too! One arm moves. When your little one presses the star on her toe, and she starts moving her hips and singing one of three different songs and twirls around, they will want to dance along with her.
One thing I noticed though, is that two of the illustrations show her in a different outfit, but that isn't part of this doll. Her outfit is not removable. She is a show stopper for little ones.
